Back up and restore Postgres clusters: base backups from 9.6 on, and from 14 on the WAL streamed through a replication slot, each in a set of its own

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres <command>
```

## postgres base

base connects as libpq does: through --dbname, or through PGHOST, PGUSER and the other PG*
variables. The user needs the REPLICATION attribute. From Postgres 15 on, goback takes the backup over
a replication connection of its own; before that, or with --pg-basebackup, pg_basebackup takes it.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres base [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dbname value` | connection string the backup connects with | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_DBNAME` |  |
| `--pg-basebackup value` | take the backup with this pg_basebackup, whose major version must match the server's | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_BASEBACKUP` |  |

## postgres receive

receive connects as a replica, as libpq does: through --dbname, or through PGHOST, PGUSER and the
other PG* variables. The role needs the REPLICATION attribute, and pg_hba.conf a replication line for it
and a line for a normal connection to the database --dbname names, postgres by default. The slot holds
WAL the receiver hasn't committed; set max_slot_wal_keep_size to bound it. Run --drop-slot when retiring
the receiver.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres receive [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--spool value` | directory WAL waits in for its commit | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_SPOOL` |  |
| `--base-set value` | set the cluster's base backups go to |  |  |
| `--dbname value` | connection string the receiver connects with | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_DBNAME` |  |
| `--slot value` | the physical replication slot; goback_ and the set's name by default |  |  |
| `--commit-every value` | how often new WAL is committed; at least 10s |  | `1m0s` |
| `--commit-bytes value` | how much new WAL makes the receiver commit early |  | `256MiB` |
| `--window value` | how far back point-in-time recovery reaches; WAL older than the oldest base backup inside it is let go |  | `336h0m0s` |
| `--allow-uncapped-slot` | stream even when max_slot_wal_keep_size lets the slot keep WAL until the database's disk is full |  |  |
| `--shutdown-grace value` | how long the last commit may take after SIGTERM |  | `30s` |
| `--drop-slot` | drop the replication slot and exit |  |  |

## postgres restore

restore_command runs goback again for every WAL file Postgres asks for: this binary with the
global flags given here, unless --goback names another command. Flags end up in
postgresql.auto.conf, or recovery.conf before Postgres 12; settings from the environment have to
be in Postgres's environment.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres restore [flags] <data directory>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--base-set value` | set the cluster's base backups go to; digits name it by id, from the set's head rather than the index |  |  |
| `--wal-set value` | set the cluster's WAL goes to, for recovering past the end of the base; digits name it by id, as --base-set |  |  |
| `--at value` | moment to recover to, as RFC 3339 (2026-10-02T14:30:00Z); the end of the WAL set when empty |  |  |
| `--goback value` | command restore_command runs goback as, global flags included |  |  |

## postgres wal-get

write a WAL file of a WAL commit to a path, as restore_command

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres wal-get [flags] <%f> <%p>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--wal-set value` | set the WAL commit belongs to |  |  |
| `--commit value` | the WAL commit, in hex |  |  |
